analysis.title: weekend prep ... (Brian Garrett, FICC and Equities)
key_insights: Garrett describes high volatility under the surface (single stocks, credit) against low volatility in the index. 12-month SPX implied correlation (ATMF) is about 20%, one of the lowest levels in history, so 2027 is priced as one of the most dispersive 12-month periods in the dataset.

SPX rose about 150bps and NDX about 300bps over Mon/Tue/Wed, which led participants to adopt an '8th inning' view that forced deleveraging was over. NDX then fell 140bps Thursday and 350bps Friday, forcing portfolio re-underwriting.

Contra-indicator 1: nervousness is showing up in index vol, catching up to the panic already priced in single-stock vol and credit. Index vol had refused to price contagion, and that is starting to change.
Contra-indicator 2: net exposure is rising because of 'risk off' flow. Equities were net bought overall, but mostly through short covering.
Contra-indicator 3: stocks are no longer 'crashing up'. For some of the largest companies, 2026 volatility came from the right tail, and that is no longer the case.
Contra-indicator 4: index valuations are 'catching down' to earnings. SPX is +10.7% on the year, yet forward P/E is about 19x, the lowest of 2026.
Contra-indicator 5: safe is expensive. The dividend yield factor is in the 90th percentile and the valuation factor in the 80th (10y), while momentum is in the 30th and growth in the 40th.
Contra-indicator 6: credit experts suggest AI financing needs could surprise to the downside. A smaller requirement from the bond market would ease anxiety but takes time to play out.

Contra-indicator 7: Garrett's retail-style indicators (a college friend and his father-in-law) have moved from buying every dip to asking before buying. He sees retail on the verge of change driven by agentic tools.

Prime brokerage: hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in four weeks, but largely as macro short covering. TMT was the most bought sector on the week but is still heavily sold month to date in October. Mag7 length is about at YTD highs.
Prime brokerage: GS regressed PB net exposure against SPX drawdowns and finds the current low net levels have been associated with drawdowns above 20%.

Cash desk: 'AI length is still being unwound'. The desk sold a net $4.2B of tech delta on Friday and finished the week as a net seller, reversing a mid-week buy skew, with a peak-to-trough skew of almost $10B on the week.

CTAs: SPX closed 35 handles above the medium-term threshold, while NDX closed below both the short and medium-term thresholds. Garrett expects a red sweep across equity systematics when updated Monday.
Derivatives: gamma has not repriced to the same extent as vol and skew. 0DTE straddles stayed consistently priced despite large realized index moves.

Derivatives: there is no excess variance priced for the midterms. The Wednesday SPX straddle covers AAPL earnings and the midterms, yet costs 30bps less than Friday's single-session move (150bps implied vs -180bps realized).
Derivatives: US equity vol traded almost 100 million contracts on Friday, the fourth-highest option volume session on record. Garrett guesses 130-150mm for the largest session of 2027.
Derivatives: downside vol is now more extreme than upside vol, as is normal for stocks, and skew has already repriced for this in the short run.
Year-end straddles with 42 sessions left in 2026: SPX +/-5.1%, NDX +/-7.8%, RTY +/-6.3%. Large cap vol exceeds small cap vol again.

Baskets: midterms should be a non-event at index level. The basket team has pair trades for health insurance affordability, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending and corporate tax beneficiaries.

sector_views.rationale: TMT was the most bought sector on the week by hedge funds but is still heavily sold in October month to date. Mag7 is one of the few TMT pockets where positioning kept building, with length near YTD highs.

earnings_insights: AAPL earnings fall in the Wednesday session whose SPX straddle (also covering the midterms) is priced 30bps below Friday's single-session move.
The GS one-delta desk 'earnings scorecard' email shows realized moves for crowded long and crowded short names have been extreme in both directions.
